Analysis by Richard Cowan

As the situation in Mexico continues to deteriorate, the wire services are now reporting that three Mexican police chiefs are seeking “political asylum” in the US! 

They are not really in danger of political persecution by the Mexican government. Instead they are running for their lives after two of the top law enforcement officials in Mexico were murdered – “assassinated”? – by representatives of the contraband industries. Eleven Mexican federal law enforcement officials have been murdered in just the last month. The situation is getting worse by the day. Why? 

“Drug-related violence killed more than 2,500 people last year alone in Mexico.” 

That sentence from an AP story demonstrates the fundamental conceptual problem that keeps the US – and other countries, including Mexico – from protecting their citizens and their national interests. The violence is not “drug-related” – meaning caused by people under the influence of “drugs”, as “alcohol-related” would mean caused by alcohol. These deaths were drug-prohibition-related! 

Moreover, they were not caused by the Mexican supply of “drugs”, but by US demand for “drugs.” If there was no US demand, there would not be any Mexican supply worth fighting over on our borders. 

This point is made even clearer when we realize that the prohibition related violence in Mexico has increased since the US cracked down on domestic production of meth, and the manufacturing moved south of the border. Before that, South American cocaine – that used to come by sea into South Florida – was pushed into Mexico by Reagan/Bush. And then there were the opium poppies… 

Of course, long before all of that, there would never have been any Mexican “marijuana” – if Americans had been allowed to grow their own “hemp”. We have the most advanced agricultural industry in the world, and – irony of ironies – the Canadian and Dutch cannabis industries were largely pioneered by Americans! 

If one listens to lying demagogues like Lou Dobbs, it is all Mexico’s fault.

See

Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the Costs of the Drugwar. 

and 

Lou Dobbs Plays Arthur Andersen to The Drug War’s Enron. A Week of Prohibitionist Propaganda And 91% Of His “Pseudosophisticate” Viewers Still Vote for Decrim. Of course, that is a typical American attitude. Our bases in Saudi Arabia – since removed – could not have played a role in provoking the 9/11 attacks, because we are always the innocent victims. We have to learn the difference between “justification” and “rationalization.” 

If the Moslems would all become good Christians like George Bush and Dick Cheney, we could have peace in the Middle East. If the Mexicans would just stop the smugglers, we could have a “drug-free-America.” If fantasies were reality, life would be video game. 

Game over! 

So what is our solution? Bush wants to give the Iraqi – excuse me – Mexican government more military aid – $500 million – to escalate the war on its own citizens. The Mexican Army is not trained to do police work, and there is no tradition of civil liberties in Mexico, so it will only make the situation even worse. 

As the AP reports, “Seven frontline border agents were killed in 2007, and two so far in 2008. Assaults against officers have also shot up from 335 in fiscal 2001 to 987 in fiscal 2007. 

There have been 362 assaults against officers during the first four months of 2008, according to Border Patrol statistics. The pattern has been that when more security resources are deployed along the U.S. border, violence against officers spike in response.” 

Sound familiar? 

We are going to turn Mexico into an Iraq on our doorstep, and the flow of economic refugees that we have now will become a flood of “political refugees” – ordinary citizens, who like the police chiefs, will be running for their lives. 

I love Mexico, but I am talking about America’s greatest national security interest, a stable country on our southern border. 

Unfortunately, it will be almost impossible to get an intelligent discussion of the issue in the current Presidential campaign. Just as Ron Paul was derided for saying that our bad foreign policies have disastrous consequences at home, any politician who does not blame Mexico for “drugs” will be denounced as “pro-drug” and anti-American. 

Even the anti-prohibitionist movement and libertarians – all understandably focused on the Drug War’s depredations in the US – are not paying enough attention to the consequences for our troubled neighbor. However, if we don’t talk about it no one will be making any sense at all and this way madness comes.
